c-pg-angles.label: Angle sum of a polygon
c-pg-angles.summary: The angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°. In a cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles add to 180°.

q-pg-ratio.label: Angles in a given ratio
q-pg-ratio.summary: Four angles in a ratio like 1 : 3 : 4 : 4; find the largest or smallest.

formulas.text: Sum of the angles of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°
Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles add to 180°
formulas.note: Use it as a check or as the main step when two angles are given.

q-pg-ratio.cue: 'The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio …'; find the biggest or smallest angle.
q-pg-ratio.standard: Ratio parts add to 1 + 3 + 4 + 4 = 12. One part = 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. Largest = 4 × 30° = 120°.
q-pg-ratio.fast: 360 ÷ 12 = 30 is clean, so every angle is a multiple of 30°. Only the multiples of 30 can be an answer.
q-pg-ratio.eliminate: The largest angle's share is 4/12 = 1/3 of 360° = 120°. Options that are not multiples of 30 (108°, 135°) are out; 90° is the 3-part angle.
traps: Using 180° instead of 360° (opposite angles are 180° but the whole sum is 360°).
Picking the 3-part angle (90°) as the largest.
Pairing opposite angles and getting inconsistent ratios; the question is solved from the angle sum alone.

pyqs.text: The angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 4 : 4. What is the largest angle?
solution: The four angles add to 360°, and the ratio parts add to 1 + 3 + 4 + 4 = 12.
The largest angle = 4 × 30° = 120°. (Strictly, no pairing of these angles gives opposite sums of 180°, so the question only works with the 360° sum.)
pyqs.trick: 360 ÷ 12 = 30, so every angle is a multiple of 30. Only 90° and 120° are, and 90° is the 3-part angle.

a.note: 90° is the angle with 3 parts, not the largest.

b.note: Parts of 30° give multiples of 30°, and 108° is not one.

d.note: Parts of 30° give multiples of 30°, and 135° is not one.
